data.title: Persist held intent bundles and import records across restart under the signing custody discipline

data.body:
[HIGH] Resolve the persisted RFC conflict before merge. Lines 833-841 retain the epoch side, the bn-3snfi side, and conflict markers. The file header also records the structured conflict. git diff --check reports four leftover markers, and Maw reports lifecycle:conflicted. The workspace-side blob also omits concurrent epoch corrections, so choosing either side wholesale can lose normative security semantics. Reconcile both histories, remove all conflict metadata, commit the result, rerun the gates, and re-request this review at the new target.

Risk:high failure-mode answers:
1. Failure modes: a merge can omit the bn-3snfi custody rule or discard newer epoch rules. Current merge and dossier gates also reject the target.
2. Edge cases: preserve the latest epoch corrections while adding correction 60 custody scope. Remove both the inline markers and the structured-conflict header.
3. Rollback: if reconciliation cannot preserve both histories, return to the persisted base and reapply only the bn-3snfi RFC addition.
4. Monitoring: require clean Maw lifecycle, zero git diff --check findings, and the existing custody refusal and unconfirmed-write counters after deployment.
5. Validation: rerun just check, focused bundle custody and keystore tests, Maw merge check, and a fresh exact-range Seal review. Reviewer test execution was environment-inconclusive because the sandbox maps the root directory to uid 65534, which the keystore ancestry check correctly refused.

data.body: [RISK:HIGH] Whole-range security review found no blocker. 1. Failure modes: a pre-commit custody refusal must restore registry, bundle, byte charge, imported flags, and records; a post-commit uncertainty must keep the live change, answer OutcomeUnknown, and quarantine trust decisions. 2. Edge cases: idempotent re-import, exported-then-imported bundles, rejected imports across restart, version-1 state, count and byte saturation, malformed or re-signed custody content, and adopted links without a carrying bundle. 3. Rollback: revert the complete base..target range before any version-2 state is written; after CTMSTA02 is written, a binary downgrade needs a preserved CTMSTA01 snapshot or a forward conversion because the old reader does not know CTMSTA02. 4. Monitoring: custody LaunchRefusal, custody-failed and custody-unconfirmed state, unconfirmed-write count, identity-collision count, and held-bundle quota refusals. 5. Validation: reviewed all 18 changed files and the persisted base..target range; git diff --check, conflict-marker scan, and cargo fmt --all -- --check pass. The custody, crash-oracle, tamper, replay, version, and differential tests cover the named paths, but this metadata-only review did not execute build or test commands that write artifacts. The separate risk:critical human gate remains required.
